preconditions.description: The input contains exactly n + 1 lines: the first line is n, followed by n lines describing each vertex.

preconditions.expression: all(0 <= degree <= n - 1 and 0 <= s < (1 << 16) for degree, s in degrees_and_sums)
preconditions.description: For every vertex, the degree is between 0 and n-1, and the XOR sum s is between 0 and 2^16 - 1.
The sum of all degrees is even, as required for any undirected graph.

postconditions.description: The number of edges printed matches the count m in the first line of output.

postconditions.expression: all(0 <= a < n and 0 <= b < n and a != b for a, b in edges)
postconditions.description: Every printed edge connects two distinct valid vertices within the range [0, n-1].

postconditions.expression: all(sum(1 for a, b in edges if a == v or b == v) == degrees[v] for v in range(n))
postconditions.description: For every vertex v, the number of edges incident to v in the output equals the input degree of v.

postconditions.expression: all((lambda v: 0 if degrees[v] == 0 else reduce(lambda x, y: x ^ y, (a if a != v else b for a, b in edges if a == v or b == v))) == sums[v] for v in range(n))
postconditions.description: For every vertex v, the XOR sum of its neighbors in the output equals the input XOR sum sv.
The total number of edges is exactly half the sum of degrees, ensuring no duplicate edges or self-loops are counted incorrectly.
